title: Why an index speeds up reads but slows writes
subtitle: Understand the trade-off behind database indexes
learning_objective: Explain how an index reduces lookup work and adds write-maintenance cost.

scenes.title: THE SLOW QUERY
scenes.body: A query scans millions of rows to find one user. An index can change how the database searches.

scenes.title: An index is an access path
scenes.body: A suitable index lets the database locate matching rows without scanning the whole table. The optimizer decides whether using it is worthwhile.

scenes.title: Indexes aren't free
scenes.body: Each extra index consumes storage and adds work to inserts, deletes, and some updates. Index columns that match real query patterns.

scenes.title: Example

scenes.question: Why can too many indexes hurt write performance?
options: The database must maintain them as data changes
Indexes always duplicate the whole table
scenes.explanation: The database must update relevant index structures when rows are inserted, deleted, or changed.

scenes.title: Remember this
scenes.body: Add indexes to support measured query patterns, then check the query plan and write cost.
